title: Numbers 8: The Teens (11-19 always take the genitive plural)
titleRussian: Числа 8: числа на -надцать (11-19 — всегда родительный множественного)
description: Meet the teen words одиннадцать through девятнадцать. They all share one rule: the noun goes into the genitive plural, just as it did after five. The second digit does not matter - twelve behaves like fifteen, not like two.
descriptionRussian: Знакомимся с числами 11-19: одиннадцать-девятнадцать. У всех одно правило: существительное стоит в родительном падеже множественного числа, как после 'пять'. Вторая цифра не имеет значения.
intro: The teens contain a trap that catches nearly everyone, and it catches them precisely because they have been paying attention. You have just spent three lessons learning that two, three and four behave one way. Twelve has a two inside it, visible right there in the word, and reaching for the rule you just learned is the natural move. It is also wrong. Read the whole number word before you decide anything.
rules: Numbers 11-19 are the 'teens'. Every teen number ends in -надцать (historically 'on ten').
All teen numbers take the noun in the genitive plural - the same form as 5-10.
Ignore the smaller number hiding inside a teen. Двенадцать contains два, but двенадцать книг follows пять книг, not две книги.
Endings on the noun are identical to those after 5-10: -ов on masculine consonants (пятнадцать студентов) and the zero ending on feminine -а (двенадцать книг).
Recognise the digits inside the teen word: дв-енадцать (12), пят-надцать (15), сем-надцать (17). The structure is regular once you see it.
examples: У меня одиннадцать книг. (I have eleven books.) Teens → gen pl, feminine -а drops: книг.
В классе двенадцать студентов. (There are twelve students in the class.) Teens → gen pl, masculine + -ов: студентов.
На полке пятнадцать книг. (There are fifteen books on the shelf.) Teens → gen pl, zero ending: книг.
У Антона тринадцать котов. (Anton has thirteen cats.) Teens → gen pl, masculine + -ов: котов.
В доме шестнадцать комнат. (There are sixteen rooms in the house.) Teens → gen pl, zero ending: комнат.
У меня девятнадцать машин. (I have nineteen cars.) Teens → gen pl, zero ending: машин.

tables.title: Teens + the Two Clean Gen Pl Patterns

items.promptEnglish: Recap from Lesson 7: I have six tables.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 7. After 'шесть' the noun takes the genitive plural, which is -ов on hard-consonant masculines. Today the same -ов will appear after every teen number.

items.hint: Teens take the gen pl, just like 5+.
items.explanation: Двенадцать is a teen (a -надцать numeral), and the whole 11-19 range takes the gen pl. Книга → книг (zero ending). Notice that 12 does NOT work like 2; the teens are a single group with the 5+ rule.

items.promptEnglish: There are fifteen students in the class.
items.explanation: Пятнадцать is a teen, so the gen pl rule applies, exactly like after пять: студент → студентов.
Тринадцать is a teen. Despite ending in -3, it does NOT take the gen sg form 'кота'. Teens always take the gen pl: котов. The teens rule beats the second-digit instinct.
Семнадцать is a teen, so the noun takes the gen pl. Feminine -а drops: машина → машин. Same form as пять машин.

items.promptEnglish: There are nineteen books on the shelf.
items.explanation: Девятнадцать is a teen, so книга takes the gen pl: книг. The same zero ending you used after пять, шесть, семь now works for any teen.

blanks: У меня четырнадцать _____. (I have fourteen phones.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 14 is a teen, so the noun is in the gen pl: телефонов. The gen sg form 'телефона' (used after 2-3-4) does not apply, even though 14 ends in a 4. Teens beat the second-digit instinct.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are eleven pupils in the class.
errorCorrection.explanation: Teens (11-19) all take the GENITIVE PLURAL on the noun: учеников. The teen rule extends the 5-and-up pattern: anything in 11-19 follows the gen pl rule, no matter how the teen word is built.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня двенадцать журнала в шкафу.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have twelve magazines in the cupboard.
errorCorrection.explanation: Teens take the GENITIVE PLURAL: журналов. Журнала is the gen sg, correct only after 2-4 ('три журнала') - the most tempting wrong answer, because twelve ends in 'two' in Russian, but the teens 11-14 do NOT follow the 2-4 rule.
After пятнадцать (a teen), the noun is in the GENITIVE PLURAL: собак (bare stem, typical for feminine -а nouns).

minimalPairs.explanation: 12 is a teen → gen pl: книг. The form 'книги' is the gen sg (used after 2, 3, 4); but the teens are not '10 + 2', they are a single counting group that takes the gen pl.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There are thirteen students in the class.
minimalPairs.explanation: 13 is a teen → gen pl: студентов. The form 'студента' (gen sg) belongs to the 2-3-4 rule; the teens override that, regardless of the second digit.

reviewVocab.definition: teen numerals (the 11-19 family, all ending in -надцать; all take the gen pl)
reviewVocab.example: К числам на -надцать относятся 11-19: одиннадцать, двенадцать, … , девятнадцать. Все они требуют родительного падежа множественного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: the teen suffix; historically 'на десяти' ('on ten'); fused into a single counting word
reviewVocab.example: Суффикс -надцать в слове 'двенадцать' исторически означал 'на десяти' — то есть 'два на десяти'.

reviewVocab.definition: the teens rule (all of 11-19 take the noun in the genitive plural, like 5-10)
reviewVocab.example: По правилу чисел 11-19 'двенадцать книг' имеет то же окончание у существительного, что и 'пять книг'.
